messages:
lina: Heads-up — CI started failing after we bumped tokenizers to 0.13.2 (CVE-2026-1245 fix). Multiple eng-runtime and eng-ml pipelines blocked.
rob: Can you paste the failing job and a log? :eyes:
ci-bot: failed job: restore-wheels-linux (manylinux). exit code 1. log attached:
```
Collecting tokenizers==0.13.2
  ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement tokenizers==0.13.2 (from versions: 0.10.1, 0.11.0, 0.12.1, 0.13.1)
  ERROR: No matching distribution found for tokenizers==0.13.2

Building wheels for collected packages: tokenizers
  Building wheel for tokenizers (pyproject.toml) ... error
  ERROR: Failed building wheel for tokenizers
  subprocess.CalledProcessError: command 'rustc' returned non-zero exit status 1.
```
sam: This looks like the upstream release for 0.13.2 didn't publish manylinux wheels, so pip falls back to building from source (needs rust). Our CI images don't have rust -> build fails/segfault.
anya: We hit the same on a transformers bump last month. Quick fixes: prefer binary wheels or pin to a published manylinux-compatible version. downside: pinning to 0.13.1 leaves us exposed to the CVE.
lina: Right. CVE notes the vulnerability fixed in 0.13.2 only. We need to balance security (urgent) vs rollout (CI blocked).
rob: Options:
- add prebuilt wheel to our internal artifacts and set PIP_FIND_LINKS in CI
- add rust toolchain to CI runners (longer term, bigger blast radius)
- vendor/backport patch into 0.13.1 and ship our patched wheel
Which has least surface area for immediate unblock?
sam: Fastest is uploading a prebuilt manylinux wheel to S3 and using --find-links. I have a draft script in PR #4210 that builds a wheel on ubuntu:20.04 and uploads it.
anya: I'll open a follow-up PR to set PIP_FIND_LINKS and pin to the internal wheel name (tokenizers==0.13.2+redwood1). That unblocks CI and lets us release the security patch.
lina: We should treat hosted API as high risk and prioritize. @sec-bot please log the triage decision and mitigation path so compliance knows we're not ignoring the CVE.
sec-bot: Logged: id SEC-2026-1157. Affected component: tokenization pipeline. Severity: P1 (hosted), P2 (dedicated/private). Mitigation: temporary internal wheel + CI override. Remediation path: upstream manylinux wheel or add rust to builders.
rob: Adding rust to CI is clean but will slow all builds and increase maintenance. I'd prefer short-term wheel override + medium-term upstream engagement.
sam: Plan proposed:
1) short-term (today): upload wheel to internal bucket, set PIP_FIND_LINKS in CI, merge PR #4216 to unblock.
2) medium (1–2 weeks): contact upstream to request manylinux wheel publish for 0.13.2; if not, prepare to backport patch.
3) long-term: evaluate adding rust toolchain to dedicated build images for packages that require compilation.
lina: Can we get PRs today? want to schedule release window 18:00 UTC. Security wants the hosted rollout as soon as CI green.
anya: :thumbsup: I'll target 16:30 UTC for the PR draft and tag reviewers.
rob: I'll standby to approve CI change and coordinate the artifact upload. If anyone's blocked by reruns ping me.
ci-bot: rerun queued for affected pipelines. job IDs: 8842, 8843.
